extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying commutative algebra / algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Lecture-note style exposition covering supports of modules, localization and Spec, integral extensions (Going-up/Going-down), Noether normalization, Nullstellensatz, Krull dimension and Jacobson rings. Contains definitions, propositions, theorems and exercises used as precise algebraic criteria and equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec functor and continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring map φ : R → R′ induces Spec(φ) : Spec(R′) → Spec(R) by Spec(φ)(p′) := φ^{-1}(p′); Spec(φ)(V(a)) = V(aR′), hence Spec(φ) is continuous and Spec(·) is a contravariant functor from Rings to Top spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the quotient R → R/a induces a closed embedding Spec(R/a) ↪ Spec(R) with image V(a); localization R → R_f induces an open embedding Spec(R_f) ↪ Spec(R) with image D(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed points in Spec
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.2): For R a ring and p ∈ Spec(R), the singleton {p} is closed in Spec(R) (i.e., p is a closed point) if and only if p is a maximal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This characterizes closed (Zariski) points in affine schemes: only maximal ideals give closed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful flatness and surjectivity on Spec
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.3): For a ring R and an R-algebra R′ with structure map φ, R′ is faithfully flat over R if and only if Spec(φ) is surjective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects algebraic notion of faithful flatness with a topological/geometric condition on prime spectra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-compactness of Spec(R)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.4): For any ring R, X := Spec(R) is quasi-compact: every open cover by basic opens has a finite subcover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the standard fact that 1 can be written as a finite sum of elements from the ideals whose complements cover Spec(R).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of quasi-compact opens
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.5): For X = Spec(R) and U an open subset, U is quasi-compact iff its complement is V(a) for some finitely generated ideal a (i.e., U = X \ V(a) with a finitely generated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic opens D(f) are quasi-compact; finite unions of such correspond to complements of finitely generated ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spec of Boolean ring: compact Hausdorff and clopen D(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.6): If B is a Boolean ring and X = Spec(B), then X is compact Hausdorff; a subset U ⊆ X is both open and closed iff U = D(f) for some f ∈ B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stone duality context; in Boolean rings every element is idempotent and D(f) are clopen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stone's theorem for Boolean rings
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.7): Every Boolean ring B is isomorphic to the ring of continuous functions from a compact Hausdorff space X to F2 (with discrete topology); equivalently B ≅ ring of clopen subsets of X; concretely X = Spec(B) and f ↦ D(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a topological representation of Boolean rings (Stone representation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of support of a module
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition (13.8): For an R-module M, Supp(M) := { p ∈ Spec(R) | M_p ≠ 0 }.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support measures where the module is nonzero after localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic properties of support (exact sequences, unions, relation to annihilator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.9): (1) For exact 0 → L → M → N → 0, Supp(L) ∪ Supp(N) = Supp(M). (2) For a directed union M = ∪ M_i, Supp(M_i) = Supp(M). (3) Supp(M) ⊆ V(Ann(M)), with equality if M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use localization exactness; equality with V(Ann(M)) for finitely generated modules follows from standard annihilator/localization arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilpotent elements on a module and nil(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition (13.10): x ∈ R is nilpotent on M if x^n m = 0 for some n ≥ 1 for all m ∈ M, equivalently x ∈ √Ann(M). Define nil(M) := √Ann(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates nilpotence on module to radical of the annihilator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intersection description of nil(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.11): For a finitely generated module M, nil(M) = ∩_{p ∈ Supp(M)} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses (13.9)(3) and primary decomposition style reasoning: primes in support determine nilpotents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of tensor product
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.12): For R-modules M and N, Supp(M ⊗_R N) ⊆ Supp(M) ∩ Supp(N), with equality when M and N are finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses localization: (M⊗N)_p ≅ M_p ⊗_{R_p} N_p and finite generation yields converse inclusion via Nakayama-type arguments or cited facts (10.14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of quotient by aM
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary (13.13): For ideal a and module M, Supp(M/aM) ⊆ Supp(M) \ V(a), with equality if M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from (13.12) and Ann(R/a)=a; equality for finitely generated M via Proposition 13.12.

rubrics_metrics.name: V(p) ⊆ Supp(M) when p ∈ Supp(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.14): If p ∈ Supp(M) then V(p) ⊆ Supp(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization arguments: if M_p ≠ 0 then for q ⊇ p, M_q localizes to nonzero as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of Q/Z example non-closed
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.15): For M = Q/Z as a Z-module, Supp(M) is not Zariski closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrates Supp need not be closed in general (only closed for finitely generated modules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of zero module via support
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.16): For module M, the following are equivalent: (1) M = 0; (2) Supp(M) = ∅; (3) M_m = 0 for every maximal ideal m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows that vanishing of all localizations at maximal ideals detects zero module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization exactness test at maximal ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.20): A sequence of modules L → M → N is exact iff its localization at each maximal ideal m is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exactness can be checked on localizations at maximal ideals; proof uses (13.16) to lift from local data to global exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation tested at maximal ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.21): Elements m_i ∈ M generate M iff their images generate M_m for every maximal ideal m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization reduces generation questions to local ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilocal lifting of isomorphisms for finitely presented modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.22): For semilocal A with maximal ideals m1,…,mn and finitely presented modules M,N, if M_{m_i} ≅ N_{m_i} for each i then M ≅ N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct global isomorphism by patching local isomorphisms multiplied by elements supported at complementary ideals; uses finite presentation and Chinese remainder-like arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flatness equivalences (local/global)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.23): For S a multiplicative subset and module M, the following are equivalent: (1) M is flat over R. (2) S^{-1}M is flat over S^{-1}R and over R. (3) For every maximal ideal m, M_m is flat over R_m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flatness is local and preserved under localization; proofs use localization exactness and faithful flatness criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally finitely generated/presented notions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition (13.25): M is locally finitely generated if for each p ∈ Spec(R) there exists f ∉ p such that M_f is finitely generated over R_f; similarly define locally finitely presented, locally free of finite rank, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local properties give rise to global conclusions under quasi-compactness hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global for finite generation/presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (13.26): (1) If M is locally finitely generated then M is finitely generated. (2) If M is locally finitely presented then M is finitely presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses quasi-compactness of Spec(R) to cover by D(f_i) where M_{f_i} finitely generated/presented and then patch global generators and relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of finite projective modules
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (13.27): For R-module P the following are equivalent: (1) P finitely generated and projective. (2) P finitely presented and flat. (3) P finitely presented and P_m is free over R_m for each maximal m. (4) P is locally free of finite rank. (5) P finitely generated and locally on D(f) becomes free of rank n for some n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard equivalence between finitely generated projective, locally free finite rank, and finitely presented flat modules; proofs proceed by localizing and patching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semilocal locally free implies free
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercise (13.29): If A is semilocal and P is locally free of rank n then P is free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses the fact that over a semilocal ring projective modules of constant rank are free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral extension preserves field property
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma (14.1): If R ⊆ R′ is integral extension of domains, then R′ is a field iff R is a field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: nonzero x ∈ R invertible in R′ satisfies an integral equation; multiply to show 1/x ∈ R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lying over / Going-up / Incomparability / Maximality (integral extensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (14.3): For integral extension R ⊆ R′ and prime p ⊆ R: (1) Maximality: if p′ lies over p then p′ maximal ⇔ p maximal. (2) Incomparability: two primes of R′ lying over same p are equal. (3) Lying over: there exists at least one prime of R′ lying over p. (4) Going up: given ideal a′ ⊈ p, one can choose the overprime containing a′.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundamental relationships between prime spectra under integral extensions; proofs use localization and properties of integral extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coefficients of monic factors are integral
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma (14.7): If f ∈ R[X] monic and f = g h in R′[X] with g,h monic, then coefficients of g and h are integral over R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses quotient rings by ⟨g⟩ and stepwise factor-root arguments; coefficients are symmetric polynomials in roots which are integral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality of minimal polynomial coefficients in normal domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposition (14.8): If R is a normal domain with fraction field K and L/K a field extension, and y ∈ L integral over R with minimal monic polynomial p ∈ K[X], then p ∈ R[X]; so the minimal polynomial has coefficients in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines integrality and normality (integrally closed) to force coefficients into R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-down for integral extensions when base is normal
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (14.9): If R ⊆ R′ is integral with R normal, and p ⫋ q are primes in R and q′ ⊆ R′ lies over q, then there exists p′ ⊆ q′ lying over p (i.e., going-down holds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to local case, uses characteristic/minimal polynomial arguments and integrality to show contractions behave as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal primes consist of zero-divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma (14.10): Any minimal prime of a ring consists entirely of zero-divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization at minimal prime has nilpotent maximal ideal; elements in minimal prime become nilpotent after localization hence are zero-divisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-down for flat (faithfully flat) algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (14.11): If R′ is a flat R-algebra (actually faithfully flat in stated proof) and p ⫋ q are primes of R and q′ in R′ lies over q, then there exists p′ ⊆ q′ lying over p (going-down holds for flat extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses faithful flatness to show surjectivity on Spec of localized maps, or reduction to domain/minimal prime case to find appropriate primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether Normalization Lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma (15.1): For k a field and R a finitely generated k-algebra (R = k[x1,…,xn]) and a chain a1 ⊆ … ⊆ ar of proper ideals, there exist algebraically independent t1,…,t_n ∈ R such that (1) R is module-finite over P := k[t1,…,t_n], and (2) for i = 1,…,r there exists h_i with a_i ∩ P = ⟨t1,…,t_{h_i}⟩. If k is infinite the t_i may be chosen as k-linear combinations of the x_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard constructive proof by choosing suitable linear combinations or monomials; yields polynomial subring over which R is integral/finite and controls contraction of ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weak Nullstellensatz
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (15.4): If k is a field and R is a finitely generated k-algebra which is itself a field, then R is a finite field extension of k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from Noether normalization: R finite over a polynomial subring P; if R is a field then P must be k.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal ideals correspond to k-points over algebraically closed fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary (15.5): If k is algebraically closed and R = k[x1,…,xn] is a finitely generated k-algebra with maximal ideal m, then m = ⟨x1−a1,…,xn−a_n⟩ for some a_i ∈ k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Weak Nullstellensatz: R/m is finite extension of k but algebraically closed k forces equality, giving residue coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert Nullstellensatz (radical equals intersection of maximal ideals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (15.6): For k a field and R a finitely generated k-algebra and a a proper ideal, rad(a) = ∩_{m ⊇ a} m (intersection over maximal ideals containing a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses localization and weak Nullstellensatz applied to R_f to produce maximal ideals avoiding any nonzero element not in rad(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chains of primes bounded by transcendence degree
rubrics_metrics.description: Lemma (15.8): If k is a field, R a finitely generated k-domain, and K = Frac(R) with transcendence degree d over k, then any chain of primes p0 ⫋ … ⫋ p_r satisfies r ≤ d; equality iff chain is maximal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Noether normalization to reduce to polynomial subring and compare heights via contractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull dimension definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition (15.9): The Krull dimension dim(R) is the supremum of lengths r of strictly ascending chains of prime ideals p0 ⫋ … ⫋ p_r in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard definition used throughout subsequent theorems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension equals transcendence degree for finitely generated domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (15.12): If k is a field and R is a finitely generated k-domain, then dim(R) = trdeg_k(Frac(R)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate consequence of Noether normalization and Lemma 15.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimension additivity at localization (through a prime)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corollary (15.13): For R a finitely generated k-domain and prime p, dim(R_p) + dim(R/p) = dim(R). If p is maximal then dim(R_p) = dim(R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cutting chains at p yields corresponding chains in localization and quotient; uses (15.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Catenary property for finitely generated algebras over fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorem (15.15): Over a field, any finitely generated algebra is catenary: for any two nested primes q ⊆ p there exist maximal-length chains between them and any two such chains have equal length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from dimension results and Noether normalization when reducing to domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobson ring definition and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Section (15.19): A ring R is Jacobson if for every ideal a, rad(a) equals the intersection of all maximal ideals containing a; equivalently (Scheinnullstellensatz): R is Jacobson iff (15.19.1) holds whenever a is prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that quotients of Jacobson rings are Jacobson and the nilradical equals the Jacobson radical in such rings.
